guides.name: BPC-157
guides.aka: Body Protection Compound-157, PL 14736, PL-10, Bepecin
guides.dopingStatus: Prohibited by WADA at all times (in and out of competition) under S0, non-approved substances. It was added to the list in 2022.
guides.nepalRegulatoryStatus: Not approved as a medicine anywhere, so it is not expected to be registered with Nepal's Department of Drug Administration (DDA). Under Nepal's Drugs Act 2035, drugs must be registered before they are imported or sold.

facts.label: What it is
facts.text: A lab-made chain of 15 amino acids, based on part of a protein first found in human stomach juice.

facts.label: What it was studied for
facts.text: Blood-vessel growth, tendon and tendon-to-bone repair, and healing of the gut lining. These results come from rats and cell experiments, not from people.

facts.label: Human evidence
facts.text: Very little. One small ulcerative colitis trial (reported only as a conference abstract) and three tiny pilot studies. No large human trial has shown it works or is safe.

facts.label: FDA
facts.text: Not approved by the FDA or any other regulator. FDA has raised concerns about immune reactions and peptide impurities. A 2026 FDA advisory panel vote on compounding is not an approval.

sources.title: FDA briefing document on BPC-157, Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee (July 2026)
Sikiric et al., Brain-gut axis and pentadecapeptide BPC 157 (Curr Neuropharmacol 2016, PubMed 27138887)
Chang et al., The promoting effect of pentadecapeptide BPC 157 on tendon healing (J Appl Physiol 2011, rat study, PubMed 21030672)
USADA: BPC-157 added to the 2022 WADA Prohibited List under S0

guides.name: TB-500 (thymosin beta-4 fragment)
guides.aka: Ac-LKKTETQ, a 7-amino-acid piece of thymosin beta-4
guides.dopingStatus: Prohibited by WADA at all times under S2 (growth factors). Thymosin beta-4 and its derivatives, such as TB-500, were added in 2018. It is also prohibited in horse racing.
guides.nepalRegulatoryStatus: Not approved as a medicine anywhere, so it is not expected to be registered with Nepal's Department of Drug Administration (DDA). Under Nepal's Drugs Act 2035, drugs must be registered before they are imported or sold.

facts.label: What it is
facts.text: A short lab-made piece (7 amino acids, Ac-LKKTETQ) of the natural protein thymosin beta-4. It is not the full protein.

facts.label: What it was studied for
facts.text: Thymosin beta-4 binds actin, a building block inside cells. In animal and lab studies it helped cells move into wounds. Whether TB-500 does this in people is unknown.

facts.label: Human evidence
facts.text: FDA found no human studies of TB-500. The full thymosin beta-4 protein has been tested in people, for example as eye drops, which is a different product.

facts.label: Combined with BPC-157?
facts.text: Some people combine the two, but no human or controlled study has tested the combination. Any "synergy" is unproven.

sources.title: FDA briefing document on TB-500, Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee (July 2026)
Goldstein, Hannappel & Kleinman, Thymosin beta4: actin-sequestering protein moonlights to repair injured tissues (Trends Mol Med 2005, PubMed 16099219)
Philp et al., The actin binding site on thymosin beta4 promotes angiogenesis (PubMed 14500546)
USADA: 2018 Prohibited List, thymosin beta-4 and TB-500 added under S2

guides.name: Semaglutide
guides.dopingStatus: Not on WADA's 2026 Prohibited List, but WADA monitors it to look for misuse. Athletes should check current rules with their anti-doping body.
guides.nepalRegulatoryStatus: Approved in the US (FDA) and the EU (EMA). We could not confirm its registration with Nepal's Department of Drug Administration. It is a prescription medicine: use only under a doctor's care.

facts.label: Class
facts.text: A GLP-1 receptor agonist: a copy of the gut hormone GLP-1 with a fatty-acid side chain that makes it last about a week.

facts.label: How it works
facts.text: Helps the body release insulin when blood sugar is high, lowers glucagon, slows stomach emptying, and acts on appetite areas of the brain.

facts.label: Main trial result
facts.text: In the STEP 1 trial, adults without diabetes lost about 14.9% of body weight over 68 weeks on average, compared with 2.4% on placebo, alongside diet and exercise.

facts.label: Side effects
facts.text: Common: nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting, constipation, stomach pain. Less common but serious: pancreatitis, gallbladder problems, kidney injury from dehydration. Boxed warning: thyroid C-cell tumours seen in rodents.

sources.title: Wilding et al., Once-Weekly Semaglutide in Adults with Overweight or Obesity (STEP 1, NEJM 2021; 384:989-1002)
FDA prescribing information for Wegovy (semaglutide)
EMA: Wegovy EPAR

guides.name: Tirzepatide
guides.dopingStatus: Not on the WADA Prohibited List, but covered by WADA monitoring together with semaglutide.
guides.nepalRegulatoryStatus: FDA-approved as Mounjaro (type 2 diabetes) and Zepbound (weight management). We could not confirm its registration with Nepal's Department of Drug Administration. It is a prescription medicine.

facts.label: Class
facts.text: Acts on two gut-hormone receptors: GLP-1 and GIP.

facts.label: How it works
facts.text: Raises insulin release when sugar is high, improves insulin sensitivity, lowers glucagon and slows stomach emptying.

facts.label: Main trial results
facts.text: In SURMOUNT-1, the highest dose gave 20.9% average weight loss at 72 weeks vs 3.1% on placebo. In SURMOUNT-5, tirzepatide led to more weight loss than semaglutide (20.2% vs 13.7%).

sources.title: Jastreboff et al., Tirzepatide Once Weekly for the Treatment of Obesity (SURMOUNT-1, NEJM 2022; 387:205-216)
Aronne et al., Tirzepatide as Compared with Semaglutide for the Treatment of Obesity (SURMOUNT-5, NEJM 2025; 393:26-36)
FDA: approval of Zepbound for chronic weight management (Nov 2023)

guides.name: Retatrutide
guides.dopingStatus: Prohibited in sport at all times. Unapproved drugs like retatrutide fall under WADA's S0 non-approved substances rule, in and out of competition.
guides.nepalRegulatoryStatus: Not approved as a medicine anywhere, so it is not expected to be registered with Nepal's Department of Drug Administration (DDA). Under Nepal's Drugs Act 2035, drugs must be registered before they are imported or sold.

facts.label: Class
facts.text: An experimental drug that acts on three hormone receptors: GLP-1, GIP and glucagon.

facts.label: Phase 2 result
facts.text: In a 2023 Phase 2 trial, adults with obesity lost up to 24.2% of body weight on average at 48 weeks.

facts.label: Phase 3 status
facts.text: Eli Lilly reported Phase 3 (TRIUMPH) results in 2026 and plans to apply to the FDA in 2027. It is not approved anywhere yet.

facts.label: The glucagon part
facts.text: In animals, glucagon action raised energy use. In people, studies show large drops in liver fat, but whether energy use rises in humans is still being studied.

sources.title: Jastreboff et al., Triple-Hormone-Receptor Agonist Retatrutide for Obesity: A Phase 2 Trial (NEJM 2023)
Eli Lilly: retatrutide Phase 3 TRIUMPH-2 and TRIUMPH-3 results (July 2026)
Coskun et al., LY3437943, a novel triple agonist (Cell Metabolism 2022, preclinical)

guides.name: GHK-Cu
guides.aka: Copper peptide, copper tripeptide-1, prezatide copper
guides.dopingStatus: Not named on the WADA list, and USADA lists GHK in cosmetics as not prohibited. Injected GHK-Cu is not approved anywhere, so it may fall under WADA's S0 rule. Athletes should check with their anti-doping agency.
guides.nepalRegulatoryStatus: Used as a cosmetic ingredient. Not approved as a medicine anywhere, so injectable forms are not expected to be registered with Nepal's Department of Drug Administration.

facts.label: What it is
facts.text: A tiny peptide of three amino acids bound to copper, found naturally in blood. First described by Dr Loren Pickart in 1973.

facts.label: Levels with age
facts.text: Pickart's work reports that blood levels fall with age, from about 200 ng/mL at age 20 to about 80 ng/mL at 60.

facts.label: Gene claims
facts.text: In lab data on human cancer cells, GHK changed the activity of many genes. This was a computer reanalysis by its discoverer, whose company sells GHK products. It does not show the same effects in people.

facts.label: Human evidence
facts.text: Mainly lab and animal studies, plus a few small 12-week skin-cream studies in women. Evidence for hair growth in people is weak. FDA notes limited human data for injectable GHK-Cu.

sources.title: Pickart & Margolina, Regenerative and Protective Actions of the GHK-Cu Peptide in the Light of the New Gene Data (Int J Mol Sci 2018, PubMed 29986520)
Pickart et al., GHK and DNA: resetting the human genome to health (BioMed Res Int 2014, PubMed 25302294; authors affiliated with Skin Biology)
FDA: Certain bulk drug substances for use in compounding that may present significant safety risks (GHK-Cu, injectable)
USADA: Peptides and growth hormones in cosmetics

quiz.statement: BPC-157 is an FDA-approved medicine for muscle and joint injuries.
quiz.explanation: BPC-157 is not approved by the FDA or any other regulator. Nearly all the evidence comes from rats. A 2026 FDA advisory panel vote about compounding is not an approval, and FDA has not made a final decision.
quiz.reference: FDA, Certain bulk drug substances that may present significant safety risks (2026); FDA BPC-157 briefing document (July 2026)

quiz.statement: BPC-157 and TB-500 are banned in all WADA-tested sports.
quiz.explanation: WADA prohibits BPC-157 under S0 (non-approved substances) and TB-500 under S2 (growth factors), both at all times. A first violation for these substances carries a default ban of up to four years.
quiz.reference: WADA 2026 Prohibited List; USADA athlete advisories (2018, 2022)

quiz.statement: Oral BPC-157 has been proven to work in people.
quiz.explanation: Lab tests by BPC-157's developers suggest it survives stomach juice, and it worked by mouth in rats. No human study shows that oral BPC-157 is absorbed or works.
quiz.reference: Sikiric et al., Gut and Liver 2020; FDA BPC-157 briefing document (July 2026)

quiz.statement: Semaglutide and tirzepatide work on exactly the same hormone pathway.
quiz.explanation: Semaglutide acts on the GLP-1 receptor only. Tirzepatide acts on both GLP-1 and GIP receptors. In the SURPASS-2 trial (type 2 diabetes), tirzepatide lowered blood sugar and weight more than semaglutide 1 mg.

quiz.statement: A lab certificate showing high HPLC purity proves a peptide is safe.
quiz.explanation: HPLC and mass spectrometry check purity and identity. They do not show a product is sterile, free of endotoxin, correctly dosed, safe or legal. In a 2024 study, peptides bought online claiming 99% purity failed on several of these.
quiz.reference: Ashraf et al., J Med Internet Res 2024 (doi:10.2196/65440); FDA guidance on synthetic peptide impurities (2021)
